headless.note: Framework staging is repository-owned and fail-closed offline. Command-line snesref remains headless; the native game runner intentionally treats system SDL2 as a host prerequisite and configures SDL3 fetching off.

purpose: Pinned SNESRecomp framework staged from the repository-owned source archive. UR-Recomp's permanent native build uses host SDL2, disables SDL3 source fetching, carries narrow project patches for exact neutral controller-stream replay and modern host integration, exposes the existing host-owned pause gate and live renderer VSync and desktop display-mode policy plus normalized active-monitor mode enumeration/application for modern product settings, adds an optional title-owned presentation-density callback for host-only HD composition, and exposes the framework's guest-frame APU timing lock needed by deterministic host-owned race restart. It also exposes a deferred full-session reboot seam that durably publishes SRAM and rebuilds the guest through title session_reset, snes_free + SnesInit, and RtlReadSram. It backports upstream 5ae0541 so a master-deadline LLE unwind raised inside a nested non-scheduler bridge frame propagates to the scheduler owner instead of being consumed in the gap frame, which silently skipped the bounced call (R-2026-10-04-UI-25). It also backports the runtime half of upstream ae921ee so RtlReset skips SPC-player re-initialization when the title registers no player; without it every scripted console `reset` segfaulted in RtlReset. The scaffold's game_rtl template also gains a hardware_reset hook that drops the host boot latch and stale LLE resume PC, so a console reset reboots from the reset vector instead of resuming the pre-reset main loop on reset hardware. It also exposes an optional title-owned dynamic native-widescreen gate so fixed/4:3 scenes can remain on the exact stock raster path while evidence-backed scenes widen. The desktop host also initializes and services the optional Lua TCP bridge when SNESRECOMP_LUA_PORT is set, with exact per-frame input/callback boundaries for replay tooling. ws_shadow layers can also carry a second, line-split world origin so split-screen viewports present world-keyed margins from one shared store.
